rich_summary: Bhishma recounts an ancient revelation about Vasudeva (Krishna). Brahma prays to the Supreme Lord—source even of Brahma himself—to incarnate among humans to destroy the Asuras reborn on Earth and restore cosmic order. The Lord agrees through the power of Yoga and disappears. When the gods ask who was addressed with such reverence, Brahma explains that the being is the eternal, unmanifest Supreme Self—Vasudeva—beyond beginning and end, the refuge of all existence. He foretells that the divine sages Nara and Narayana will appear among men and remain unrecognized by the ignorant. Bhishma concludes that Krishna is this supreme reality and that wherever Krishna and righteousness stand, victory must follow—hence the Pandavas will inevitably triumph.

highlight_spans.why: Establishes Vasudeva as the source even of Brahma, framing the theological hierarchy.
The plea for the Lord to incarnate among humans to destroy Asuras and restore order.
The reverent invocation urging the divine to descend for the happiness of all worlds.

top_scenes.scene_text: Brahma humbly addressing the radiant cosmic form of Vasudeva in a celestial assembly of gods and sages.
The Supreme Lord silently agreeing through Yoga and vanishing, leaving the astonished gods and Gandharvas gazing into empty divine light.
Bhishma declaring before a king that wherever Krishna stands with righteousness, victory inevitably follows.
